newsitem.title: GERMANY: Arrested Iranian editor telephones wife in Germany.
newsitem.headline: Arrested Iranian editor telephones wife in Germany.

text.p: An arrested Iranian journalist whose fate is worrying the Bonn government has telephoned his wife in Germany to say he is well, but that he expects to be convicted, the Tageszeitung daily said on Thursday.

German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel has written two letters to Iran concerning Faraj Sarkuhi, whose wife, Farideh Zebarjad, and two children live in Germany. Tehran says it arrested Sarkuhi for trying to leave Iran illegally earlier this month.
Zebarjad, in a story to be published on Friday, quotes Sarkuhi telling her from prison: "I am well, I can even listen to the radio and watch television."
He said he expected to be convicted, but did not say what for.
The telephone call was the first confirmation that Sarkuhi, editor of the monthly Adineh (Friday), was still alive since he was arrested at the end of January.
Zebarjad said earlier this week that Sarkuhi's brother Ismail, also under arrest, had contacted her to say that if she cooperated with Tehran, her husband could be released in two or three months.

He urged her to dismiss as a forgery a letter from her husband in which he alleged he was held for six weeks and tortured by the Iranian secret service in Tehran late last year to force him to confess to spying for Germany.

Zebarjad has said she fears her husband is being held as a bargaining chip to put pressure on German authorities not to convict an Iranian and four Lebanese on trial in Berlin for a 1992 assassination of Kurdish dissidents.

State prosecutors have angered Tehran by accusing the Iranian government of ordering the killings. The trial is expected to end within the next few months. Iran denies any involvement in the killings.
